newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends higher on short covering.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen contract ended Tokyo firmer on dealers' short-covering ahead of the weekend and in line with recoveries in Japanese government bonds, traders said on Friday.
Earlier, the June dipped temporarily on a vague rumour that the Bank of Japan will eventually have to tighten credit to put brakes on a further depreciation of the yen, traders said.
The June fell to a low of 99.15 on the rumour.
"The rumour appears to have been totally groundless and the June quickly recovered after early dips," said a bank trader.

In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, the rumour temporarily pushed up the three-year IRS rate by approximately two basis points. However, it came back down to the quote of 1.33/1.37 percent by 0701 GMT, little changed from 1.32/36 percent in late trading on Thursday.

The market generaly believes the Bank of Japan is unlikely to tighten credit before the middle of 1997 as it has to see the possible impact on the economy of a planned consumption tax increase to five percent from the current three in April.
